title: He stood in front of fire…
paragraphs:
He stood in front of fire…
and felt colder than ever.

Because when God calls you—
it doesn’t always feel like power.
Sometimes… it feels like exposure.

Moses saw the burning bush.
Flames dancing.
Branches alive but not consumed.
Holy.
Unexplainable.
Undeniable.
You would think that moment would ignite courage.
But it didn’t.
It exposed fear.
In Exodus 3–4, God speaks clearly:

“I have seen the suffering of My people…
I am sending you.”

Not a suggestion.
A commission.
And Moses?
He starts pulling back layer after layer of resistance.
“Who am I?”

That’s not humility.
That’s insecurity talking loud.

“I’m not enough.”
“I don’t belong in that room.”
“I can’t carry that weight.”
Sound familiar?
Then he says:
“What if they don’t believe me?”
Now it’s rejection.

Because it’s one thing to hear God—
it’s another to face people.
The fear of being dismissed, laughed at, questioned.
So Moses stalls.
Then he goes deeper:
“I’m not eloquent.”
Now it’s inadequacy.

He’s not just afraid of the mission—
he’s afraid of how he’ll look doing it.
Because calling often puts you where your weakness is most visible.
And finally… the raw truth breaks out:
“Please, Lord… send someone else.”
There it is.
Not confusion.
Not lack of evidence.
Just fear… dressed as an excuse.
Let’s not pretend we’re different.

We don’t stand in deserts with burning bushes—
but we’ve all had moments where God nudged us.

Speak.
Forgive.
Lead.
Repent.
Step out.
And instead of moving… we calculate.
Delay.
Deflect.
Why?
Because calling is costly.

It pulls you out of hiding.
It confronts your past.
It demands surrender.
And Moses had a past.

A man he killed.
A life he ran from.
An identity he buried in the wilderness.

So when God said, “Go back to Egypt,”
He wasn’t just sending Moses to Pharaoh.
He was sending him back to the place of his failure.

Some scholars interpret Moses’ hesitation as trauma resurfacing—an exile forced to face the land he escaped. Others see it as humility that slipped into fear. But Scripture makes one thing unmistakable:
God never withdraws the call.
And here’s the turning point that changes everything:
God doesn’t argue with Moses’ weakness.
He answers it with His presence.
“I will be with you.” (Exodus 3:12)
Read that again.

God didn’t say, “You’re strong enough.”
He didn’t say, “You’ll figure it out.”
He said, “I’m going with you.”
That’s the difference.

Calling is not about your capability.
It’s about God’s presence.
But don’t miss this—

God does get angry in Exodus 4:14.
Not because Moses is weak…
But because Moses keeps resisting after God has already promised Himself.
There’s a line between honest fear and hardened refusal.
And Moses was getting close.
Yet even there—grace shows up.

God sends Aaron.
God provides signs.
God stays faithful.
Because when God calls, He also carries.
Now here’s where the story crashes into us.
Because Moses isn’t the only one who struggled to say yes.
We all have our burning bush moments.
Moments where God interrupts our normal and says:

“Come closer.”
“Take off your sandals.”
“This is holy ground.”
And we feel it—

That tension between what is safe…
and what is sacred.
But the greater story doesn’t end with Moses.
It points forward.
To a better obedience.
A perfect surrender.
Jesus Christ faced His own moment in a garden.
Not a burning bush—
But crushing weight.
Not a command to go to Pharaoh—
But a cross.
And where Moses said, “Send someone else…”
Jesus said:
“Not My will, but Yours be done.” (Luke 22:42)
That’s the Gospel.

Where we hesitate—He obeyed.
Where we shrink back—He stepped forward.
Where we run—He stayed.
All the way to the cross.

For your fear.
For your excuses.
For your sin.
So now when God calls you—
It’s not a threat.
It’s not pressure.
It’s an invitation grounded in grace.

Because the One who calls you…
already died for you…
already rose for you…
already walks with you.
You don’t have to be fearless.
You just have to be willing.
Maybe your “Egypt” is a conversation you’ve been avoiding.
Maybe your “Pharaoh” is a habit you refuse to confront.
Maybe your calling feels too big, too heavy, too exposing.
And deep down, you’ve been whispering:
“Lord… send someone else.”
But what if He’s still saying:
“I will be with you.”

Not when you’re perfect.
Not when you’re ready.
Not when you feel strong.
Now.
This is your moment.

Not dramatic.
Not loud.
But real.
Will you keep running?

Or will you finally turn…
step closer to the fire…
and say yes?
Pause.
Pray.
Respond.
Because delayed obedience is still resistance.
And God’s call doesn’t disappear—it waits.
Step into it.
Even trembling.
Especially trembling.

Because the same God who met Moses in the wilderness
is meeting you right here.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
